statement: SUPPLEMENT, registered 2026-11-02 (the day before the election, before any result exists): an EXTERNAL benchmark. On Point Politics (onpointpolitics.us) published county-level forecasts for all five Missouri measures; their 2026-11-02 pages were captured (raw HTML, full-page screenshots, Wayback Machine copies; hashes in onpoint_benchmark_evidence_2026-11-02.csv). Their county pattern is partisanship plus demographics (age, education, race, density) plus polls; ours adds each county's own issue-voting record. H: the registered county pattern beats theirs. Secondary to the 2026-10-14 H1, which it does not replace.
metric: skill_vs_onpoint = 1 - RMSE_ours/RMSE_onpoint over 5 measures x 115 jurisdictions. Their share = their county Yes/(Yes+No) from the 'Every county' table, flipped to No/(Yes+No) where our progressive side is NO (Amendments 3, 7, 8, Proposition A = the map referendum). Joined on FIPS (their 29510 is St. Louis City despite its label). Kansas City (2938000) is folded into Jackson (29095) for ours and for the certified result, vote-weighted by 2026 votes cast on the measure. Ours, theirs and the partisanship-only baseline are each relevelled to the certified statewide share (scoring.relevel, weights = 2026 votes cast) before errors are taken.
ex_ante_call: skill_vs_onpoint > 0 with the 95% county-blocked bootstrap interval excluding 0
scoring: County-blocked bootstrap: resample the 115 jurisdictions with replacement (all five measures travel together), 10,000 draws; report the point estimate, 95% percentile interval and share of draws <= 0. Report per-measure skill too, and On Point's own skill vs the partisanship-only baseline. Interval excludes 0 above = ours better; excludes 0 below = theirs better; straddles 0 = no difference shown. Reported win or lose.

statement: SUPPLEMENT, registered 2026-11-02: where the two models disagree most. After relevelling, take the Amendment 3 jurisdictions where our predicted No share and On Point's differ by at least 5 points (e.g. Clark County: ours 38.9%, theirs 26.3% before relevelling). The question the False Bastion idea stands on: does a red county's 2024 issue gap survive into 2026, or fall back to its label?
metric: share of those jurisdictions where the certified No share is closer to our relevelled prediction than to theirs
scoring: One-sided exact binomial test against 0.5, alpha 0.05; report the count of disagreement jurisdictions (if fewer than 10, report descriptively only, no test). Report the same for all five measures pooled as a secondary line.

statement: SUPPLEMENT, registered 2026-11-02: the statewide level calls side by side, descriptive only (five measures is too few for a test). Their headline 'Forecast Yes' (A3 48.2, A6 54.7, A7 66.6, A8 75.9, Prop A 49.3) and the sum of their own county table (49.8, 53.4, 67.7, 76.4, 51.2) differ by up to 2 points; both are recorded.
metric: absolute error vs the certified share for our level_central, their headline Forecast Yes, and their county-table sum (all on the progressive side)
scoring: Table per measure, plus pass/fail called correctly for each. Largest pre-registered disagreement: Amendment 7 (ours 58% No = fails; theirs 66.6% Yes, 93.9% to pass).
